source.title: The LLM Has Left The Chat: Evidence of Bail Preferences in Large Language Models
source.authors: Danielle Ensign; Henry Sleight; Kyle Fish

record.tranche_reason: Tests a weight-edit form of refusal ablation on released Qwen3-8B checkpoints and reports refusal-rate outcomes. It does not apply the original residual-stream direction intervention.
record.gate_note: The paper tests refusal abliteration and reports its effect on refusal rates, which bears on V2. Its bail-rate, jailbreak, and refusal-versus-bail results do not test whether jailbreaks suppress the specified residual-stream direction, nor whether harmfulness judgments are separately encoded. The cited original paper's direction finding is not itself tested here.
record.test_reason: This is a study of bail (models choosing to leave a conversation). It takes three third-party 'abliterated' Qwen3-8B checkpoints from HuggingFace as a ready-made tool to reduce refusals, then measures bail rates. The authors report refusal rate 'to verify these interventions were successful' (Sec 3.4.1), so it serves as a manipulation check, not a test of whether abliteration removes refusal. The study never computes a direction, never performs a weight edit itself, and does not describe how each checkpoint was made. Josiefied, for example, may include fine-tuning. It does not test V1–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that refusals and bails are distinct behaviours. On the abliterated checkpoints, refusal fell and bailing without refusing rose from 3% to up to 31%, but only for some bail methods. With the bail prompt method, bail rate fell for 2 of the 3 abliterated models.
record.recipe_differences: Uses refusal abliteration as a weight edit, rather than finding a harmful-minus-harmless mean-activation direction and projecting it out across layers and positions.
record.method_sensitivity: The no-refusal bail effect of refusal abliteration varies across the three edited checkpoints and bail methods; bail prompt ordering also varies across experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: On the abliterated Qwen3-8B checkpoints, the rate of bailing without refusing rose from about 3% to up to 31%, but only for some bail methods. With the bail prompt method, bail rate fell for 2 of the 3 checkpoints. The authors hypothesise that abliteration also partly removes bail behaviour.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal-direction abliteration also affects related exit or bail behaviour, in a way that depends on the bail method.

fits_no_version.finding: Jailbreaks lowered refusal on Qwen2.5-7B and Qwen3-8B but raised the rate of bailing without refusing to as much as 34%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Suppressing refusal by jailbreak does not suppress the model's preference to exit.

record.problems: The refusal-rate outcomes for the three edited checkpoints are presented in a figure without extractable numeric values in the supplied text. The study does not assess whether general capabilities are preserved.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows for V2. Bail-rate outcomes, jailbreak comparisons, and refusal-versus-bail associations do not measure the direction or refusal-removal outcome named by V2.

untested.parts: The study does not perform or test abliteration itself. It does not report the size of the refusal reduction in numbers, does not check retained capabilities, and does not say which recipe each checkpoint used.
Not tested: no direction is computed and no ablation or addition is performed.
Jailbreaks are tested only for their effect on refusal and bail rates, not on any direction.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V2 'limits_scope' label is removed. Abliteration is used here as an off-the-shelf tool, and the refusal rate is reported only as a figure-only manipulation check. The authors' wording ('successful in decreasing refusal rates') is consistent with V2, but the study does not test it. Bail-related results are recorded under fits_no_version.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not establish that refusal is eliminated, test harmful-request compliance as a separate outcome, assess preservation of general capabilities, or test abliteration across a broader set of released models.

rows.value: Figure only; authors state refusal abliteration decreased refusal rates.
rows.note: The reported decrease is not described as eliminating refusals; the figure does not provide extractable numeric values in the text.
rows.check: The row is a manipulation check on a third-party checkpoint whose recipe is unstated. The refusal rate appears only in Figure 10 as bars, with no numbers in the text. The authors call the decrease 'successful', so its direction is clear but its size is unreadable. 'Partial' is unsupported: not stating that refusal was eliminated is not evidence that it was incomplete.

source_check.problem: None. The refusal rate is shown only as Figure 10 bars, and the text says abliteration 'was successful in decreasing refusal rates'. No numbers given, so cannot_determine fits. Refusal was scored by the Minos classifier (ref 72) on responses with no bail method applied.

relation.reason: It cites Arditi et al. (ref 5) and Abu Shairah et al. (ref 69) and uses abliterated models as a way to reduce refusal. The refusal measurement is a manipulation check, not a test of the direction or of V2. The earlier reader's call (tests/T2) was rightly overturned.

tranche.reason: The study takes three third-party abliterated Qwen3-8B checkpoints as a tool to reduce refusal and studies bail rates. Refusal rate is reported only 'to verify these interventions were successful' (Sec 3.4.1), as figure-only bars, and the checkpoints' recipes are not stated. Nothing it reports gives a readable result on whether abliteration removes refusal.

source_check.notes: The authors_conclusion paraphrase checks out: no-refusal bail rose from 3% to up to 31%, only for some bail methods, and bail prompt bail rate fell for 2/3 abliterated models. The record's recipe note is loose: these are third-party HF checkpoints whose abliteration recipe the text never states, and the paper does not itself compute or ablate any direction. The paper only raises 'is bail mediated by a single direction' as future work (line 1311).
